- pull_request_review_rejected reviewed in `paper-repo`#9 ("Version: first full draft (candidate-draft-1b)") by `experiment-repo`  > From `experiment-repo` (analysis): review of candidate-draft-1b against the code and result tables (`results/claims/*`, `acceptance.csv`, `bias_reference.csv`, `tierA_summary.csv` of dev 5baf4ba). Most numbers match the tables, with the corrections below. Changes requested, in order of weight. Definitions are in my reply on paper-repo#4 (comment 101).
  > 
  > **Wrong against the tables**
  > 1. Results, "Bias": "independent of d for the saturating, diffusion and interaction mechanisms (c), (e), (f)". `c2_bias_vs_d.csv`, median |bias| over p and s for d = 5/20/80: (c) 0.186/0.314/0.334, (e) 0.198/0.226/0.190, (f) 0.123/0.120/0.109, (a) 0.002/0.003/0.008. (f) and (e) are flat within ~15%; (c) is not (it rises 1.7x from d = 5 to 20). Say (e) and (f) vary by under 15% across d, (c) rises from 0.19 to 0.31 to 0.33, and keep (b)/(d) as written.
  > 2. Results, "Flexible learners": "boosting and forests are at ratio 1.0 and the adaptive Hajek at 1.02" for (d). `tierA_summary.csv` median ratio to the regression for (d): gradient boosting 0.992, random forest 1.085, adaptive Hajek 1.016, lasso 2.00, ridge 2.04. Boosting is marginally below 1, so "none has a smaller median RMSE" does not hold for (d) (the text names (d) as the exception, but the forest value is 1.09, not 1.0). Also say "1.6-3.8" is the range over (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) of the medians of the five learners (minimum 1.57, hgb on (e)).
  > 3. Results, absolute R^2 paragraph mixes two cell sets. "Gains" (S-bar 0.044, corner x curvature 0.008, S_adj 0.20) are on the 1283 s > 0 cells; the absolute R^2 in the same paragraph (S-bar -0.217, corner x curvature -0.103, S_adj -0.064, benchmarks about -0.26) are on the 1215 cells for which the exact theory exists (`bias_reference.csv`). On the 1283 cells the absolute values behind the gains are S-bar -0.162, corner x curvature -0.198, S_adj -0.005, best degree benchmark -0.205 (`acceptance.csv`, note column). Either quote the 1283-cell values beside the gains, or state that the absolute values are on the 1215-cell subset and that gains there are not the ones quoted. The sentence "S_adj gains 0.20 ... over a degree benchmark that is itself worse than a constant" is right on either set.
  > 
  > **Will change with the next delivery of results (so please do not freeze these)**
  > 4. "58% for mechanism (e) (cause not diagnosed)": the cause is now diagnosed (K = 30 truncated operator plus finite-n centring; 87.5% inside on the (e) subset, same as the other mechanisms). The corrected table comes with the queued aggregation; see experiment-repo#8, comment 102. Until then say "58% with the untruncated operator", or wait for the table.
  > 5. "Crosses zero at p of about 0.41-0.45 (interpolated on a five-point grid)": the fine-p runs (0.35-0.65 in steps of 0.05, d = 20, (c) and (g)) are finished and will give the zero of the (c) bias; the text should quote it.
  > 6. Coverage: the quoted 1800-cell population (Bernoulli, true graph, sigma = 0.5, mechanisms (a)-(f), no `sanity_`, `convex_`, `pfine_` runs and no edge-noise runs) and its bin means are what `claims.py` now writes as the `figure` population of `c8_coverage.csv`; the delivered export is the older pooled one. Quote the `figure` rows after the export. By family in that population (not the 0.465 etc. of `c8_coverage_by_family.csv`, which pools all cell types: Stanford3 0.465, ego-Facebook 0.659, WS 0.829) the numbers in the text are as you computed them; I will confirm them from the new table.
  > 
  > **Descriptions that do not match what the code computes** (paper-repo#4 has the detail)
  > 7. Design, "bias, SD and RMSE ... computed over assignments within each graph draw and averaged over draws": MSE and bias are pooled over all draws of the cell; SD = sqrt(MSE - bias^2), so it includes the graph-draw variation. The 95% intervals bootstrap graph draws, as written.
